# Public manifest wire-format clarification v1

This is a declarative public API description derived by Coordinator source inspection, without executing or importing the builder. It supplies no builder implementation to the independent author. The frozen case-generation specification remains the authority for all mathematical values, controls, malformed mutations and coverage; this document fixes their transport format only.

Serialization: one UTF-8 JSON object, object keys sorted lexicographically at every level, compact separators comma and colon with no spaces, default JSON ASCII escaping, no NaN/Infinity, followed by exactly one newline. Arrays retain their specified order. Duplicate object keys are forbidden. The materializer uses exclusive binary creation, flush and fsync; its returned receipt describes the actual bytes, not an extra object embedded in the manifest.

Top-level exact keys:
- schema: literal "prime-scalar.typed-manifest/v1".
- spec_sha256: literal "7f68929cedcf12965554d96eefe7b1aeddef82f0f1bb182e6e37113e16d5e9dc".
- counts: object with exact keys base_cases,base_depth_queries,valid_entry_calls,malformed_entry_calls,total_entry_calls,oracle_full_evaluations. Values are nonnegative JSON integers (not booleans). The first five are649,1680,23824,128,23952. oracle_full_evaluations equals sum overcases len(generators)*(2^(n+1)-1); independently recompute, never trust the field.
- cases: ordered array of649base case objects.
- calls: ordered array of23952call objects. No separate malformed-cases array.

Exhaustive case objects have exactly id,family,p,n,assignment,generators. id is "case-" plus zero-padded minimum-width4decimal global base-case index, starting case-0000. These exhaustively generated cases occupy indices0through639. family is the locked family identifier; p,n,assignment are ordinary JSON integers. generators is a JSON array of polynomials, each polynomial an array of [mask,coefficient] integer pairs in ascending mask order; zero coefficients omitted; zero polynomial is[], empty generator list is[]. This case-level representation is NOT a typed tree.

The final nine control case objects preserve EVERY field from the corresponding locked spec controls object, except id becomes "control-" plus the spec's original id, and family is added as "control". No other fields are dropped or invented. Thus controls may have expected,scope,projected_bits_context_only,restriction_depth2_dictionary_deletes,expectation_provenance exactly where the spec does. Compare each control's exact keyset/values against its spec counterpart with these two substitutions; do not apply the exhaustive-case six-key restriction to controls. Controls are in spec order, after exhaustive cases. Their case-level generators remain the exact spec pair order.

Every call object has EXACT keys id,case_id,family,order,container,repeat,api,depth,malformed,arguments.
- id is "call-" plus zero-padded minimum-width5decimal global call index, contiguous call-00000 through call-23951.
- Valid calls: case_id references an existing base case, family equals its family; order is "ascending" or "descending"; container is "list" or "tuple"; repeat is integer0or1; api is "extract_reference","extract_sweep" or "restrict_reference"; malformed is JSON false. depth is JSON null for extraction and an ordinary JSON integer0..n for restriction. arguments is a typed LIST containing p,n,assignment,generators, and an additional depth only for restriction.
- Each valid case has the fixed order: ascending then descending mask insertion; list then tuple container; repeat0then1; extract_reference,extract_sweep,then restrict_reference depths0..n. Dictionary entries follow declared mask insertion order; the outer generators container has its declared list/tuple tag. All23824valid calls precede malformed calls.
- Malformed call case_id is "malformed-global-" plus two-digit mutation index00..19, or "malformed-depth-" plus index00..03. These are NOT references into cases. family is respectively "malformed-global" or "malformed-depth"; order="ascending",container="list",repeat0or1,malformed=true. The label container remains "list" even when the malformed argument replaces the generators value with a dict or None.
- Malformed order: global mutations in spec order, then depth mutations; within each mutation repeat0then1; global APIs reference,sweep,restriction, depth mutations restriction only. Each starts from the spec's registered malformed base, applies that one specified mutation and no other alteration. arguments is typed LIST of4or5arguments by API.
- IMPORTANT depth asymmetry: on malformed restriction calls, the call.depth field is itself a TYPED scalar node (including ["int","0"] for global mutations); on malformed extraction calls it is JSON null. It is not the ordinary JSON integer used by valid restriction calls. Check that typed depth agrees with the final typed argument. Preserve bool/float malformed depth tags.

Typed tree emitted for arguments and malformed restriction depth:
- None: ["none"] (one element).
- Exact bool: ["bool",true] or ["bool",false].
- Exact int: ["int",canonical decimal string], including negatives for malformed values. No bool/int collapse or numeric JSON payload.
- Exact float: ["float",Python float.hex string] (for fixed spec values,2.0="0x1.0000000000000p+1",1.0="0x1.0000000000000p+0",0.0="0x0.0p+0").
- Exact list/tuple: ["list",array_of_typed_children] or ["tuple",array_of_typed_children].
- Exact dict: ["dict",array_of_[typed_key,typed_value]_pairs], retaining insertion order. Empty dict is["dict",[]].
No string typed node is emitted or accepted by this builder's typed-value interface; strings in manifest labels/spec-control annotations are ordinary JSON strings, outside typed arguments. The broader harness typed-tree description mentions a string tag, but this locked materializer never needs it; do not invent a string-argument case.

Malformed replacement semantics are fixed by the spec: p/n/assignment value replacement; generators becomes empty dict for its symbolic empty-dict mutation, otherwise the specified value; generator0's list mutation becomes [[1,1]]; mask mutation gives a single dict entry with the exact typed mutated mask and coefficient1; coefficient mutation gives mask1 and the exact typed mutated coefficient. The bool-key case remains a bool typed key because it is the sole inserted key; no collision with an existing integer key is introduced. Do not normalize these cases into valid dictionaries.

Materialize return receipt exact keys: metadata_admission (the supplied nonempty reference),sha256(actual manifest payload),bytes(actual payload length),counts(the manifest counts object). This return value is not native authority and is not automatically written as a separate receipt file. The admitted driver/supervisor must preserve it with actual source/native/resource evidence.

Independent audit must use the frozen spec and declarative shape above, not this description as a substitute for exhaustive value/ordinal verification. No candidate or oracle invocation is needed for the metadata audit. This clarification changes no cases, counts, algorithms, budgets or permission boundaries.

# Public native authority interface clarification v1

Declarative interface derived by Coordinator read-only inspection of tools/goal_lanes.py and existing records, not by executing/importing it. Native formats below already exist. The proposed metadata-phase approval format below does NOT yet exist and requires reviewed source plus exact Coordinator publication before use.

## Existing native paths and records

Repository root: /home/ec2-user/crypto-prime-sat-ideas-20261029.
Queue: coordination/goals/GOAL-PFDR-fd09e0/batches/BATCH-a99822/dispatch_queue.json.
Claims directory: coordination/goals/GOAL-PFDR-fd09e0/batches/BATCH-a99822/claims/.
Claim filename: TASK-ID.EPOCH.claim.json; release filename: TASK-ID.EPOCH.release.json. EPOCH is a positive integer. All claim/release records are write-once; no editing, renewal in place or overwriting.
Current task identities: source TASK-20261107-57cb8a; metadata TASK-20261107-e7cdd2; snapshot TASK-20261107-969bcf. Source and metadata are different claims; source approval is not metadata execution authority. The initial DEC-20261107-7fec0c admits source only and leaves metadata blocked.

Native claim schema string: crypto.autoresearch.task_claim.v1.
Fields emitted by native creation: schema,task_id,epoch,owner,session,branch,worktree,acquired_at,expires_at,write_scope,supersedes,forced,supersedes_lost_completion.
- task_id and owner are strings; epoch exact positive integer; timestamps UTC ISO8601, native emitted form YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ; write_scope is path-string list.
- session can be null; branch/worktree identify provenance. Supersedes values may be null or structured historical metadata; do not infer authority from them. forced is boolean, and supersedes_lost_completion may be null.
- owner is a research actor label, NOT an OS username or cryptographic identity. Verify actual caller OS UID/worktree separately against the exact phase approval; do not compare UID to owner string.

Native release schema string: crypto.autoresearch.task_release.v1.
Fields emitted: schema,task_id,epoch,owner,outcome,released_at,was_expired,note,artifact_sha256.
- outcome is completed,failed or abandoned; note may be null; artifact_sha256 maps exact repository-relative artifact paths to SHA256hex. was_expired is a boolean recording native classification at release.
- A completed release is evidence of task disposition, not proof of scientific correctness. For this source phase require exact four artifact bindings and published bytes, no expired source completion under this contract.

## Native fencing semantics and stricter execution gate

Native discovery can read local claim files and known Git refs; local copies take precedence because records are expected write-once. Highest observed epoch wins. At that epoch: missing claim with release is orphan_release; matching-owner release gives released; a release whose owner differs from the claim is foreign_release and does NOT release the valid holder. With no valid release, now>=expires_at is expired, otherwise live. Equality at expiry is not live. Native releases are allowed to record expired outcomes; this metadata execution gate requires an actually live metadata claim and timely source completion.

Supervisor must parse these exact structures, fence task+epoch+owner, reject malformed/orphan/ambiguous histories, and never accept a lower epoch. For safety it may refuse any foreign-release ambiguity, but must not treat a foreign release as valid completion. Require no valid metadata release, current time before expires_at, and enough residual claim/phase deadline for planned bounded work. Recheck before reservation and gate release. Source release must match source claim owner/epoch and exact source SHA map, have outcome completed, was_expired=false and released_at<=source expires_at. Later source epochs invalidate a stale selected completion unless an explicit new disposition binds them.

Root supplies a fresh native readiness result obtained through tools/research_dispatch.py QUEUE --ready-only --claims local (or refs after authoritative reconciliation). This is a readiness observation, not standalone authorization. Native queue raw state may remain queued while actual claims/release overlay makes a dependency completed. Do not require raw source state==completed as the only acceptable evidence. Metadata must no longer be blocked under an explicitly approved guarded transition, then have actual live claim.

Do not run --ready-only repeatedly inside a5sparent startup budget: root captures native readiness before launch; supervisor checks exact published authority and current local/known-ref fencing. No finite local scan proves absence of an unseen remote claim; root is responsible for fresh fetch/reconciliation before dispatch. If this freshness premise is unavailable, refuse launch. This is native cooperative ownership under trusted local operator/repository permissions, not hostile-same-UID isolation.

## Authoritative Git binding and managed queue

For each relevant published DEC, claim, release, source artifact, static-review receipt and phase approval, bind exact40hex commit and repository-relative path. Read actual Git blob bytes at COMMIT:path, SHA256 them and compare with the trusted publication-bound expected digest. Verify commit exists, is ancestor of approved fetched upstream/current worktree ancestry, and root retained exact GitHub repository commit readback. Local dirty bytes or a caller-supplied arbitrary JSON are not publication evidence. Effective runtime source bytes must equal those published bytes; prevent path/symlink/digest-to-import substitution. Source maps must include driver,supervisor,auditor,audit-contract.

The dispatch queue is a managed artifact, not necessarily a direct Git blob. Its containing directory's .artifacts.json and .gitignore are committed; root uses native tools/artifacts/artifacts.py push/verify to hydrate/verify it. Never assume git show COMMIT:dispatch_queue.json works, never force-add the ignored queue, and do not pretend a local hash alone proves publication. Phase approval must bind exact hydrated queue SHA plus its published managed-artifact descriptor and native remote-verification receipt. Root performs actual managed storage verification before launch; supervisor checks current hydrated bytes against the bound digest and exact task scope/state. The claim/release JSON and source/DEC files are ordinary Git blobs.

A Git commit or GitHub existence check alone does NOT establish that a record was approved by the Coordinator; the trusted operator must select the exact approved path/hash/commit in the launch binding. The supervisor checks that selected record and corresponding committed Coordinator DEC, not any document claiming approved_by=coordinator. This remains the repository's existing trusted-operator authority model; do not invent a signature verifier or assert malicious-writer protection.

## Future metadata phase approval: newly defined, not native-existing

Reserve one exact public path for future reviewed publication:
coordination/prime_scalar_manifest_metadata_20261107/metadata-phase-approval.json.
Proposed schema name: prime-scalar.metadata-phase-approval/v1. This name/format is a new local contract the author may specify in audit-contract.json; it is NOT an existing goal_lanes or research_dispatch schema and no actual approval record exists yet. Require publication by root after Coordinator review; initial source DEC does not authorize it.

Minimum explicit fields to define and validate in source: schema; phase identifier; execution scope metadata_only; exact metadata task/owner/epoch and source task; approved_by Coordinator and actual immutable approving decision reference; issued/expiry times; approved caller UID/repository/worktree; exact published source/spec/builder/interface/static-review bindings; source claim/release binding; guarded queue managed-publication binding; public mapping_v1 clarification binding; builder/audit single-use reservation paths and allowed fresh output paths; independent onebuilder+oneaudit limits; sharedslice/parent/worker names/nonce identity; exact interpreter/command/environment; byte limits; source-before-metadata dependency and no-candidate/no-oracle rule. Define precise types and canonical paths; no loose optional-field defaults granting permission.

Root launch provides an exact phase-approval path, SHA256 and published commit through the trusted approved invocation, plus exact approving DEC path/hash/commit. Author must implement validation of those values, not create a record itself or accept arbitrary boolean true. The author may define a strict runtime-binding schema for these launch inputs, but actual values remain unresolved until source/static review and Coordinator phase approval. Expose gaps explicitly; metadata remains blocked while any authority/resource field is unresolved.

Root must publish the actual metadata claim after readiness, then bind it in the trusted launch invocation; no need for a circular approval hash that contains the hash of its own future claim. Approval can fix allowed owner/task and claim policy, while launch binding fixes actual published epoch/claim bytes; supervisor must require agreement and freshness. Similarly do not require approval commit to contain its own hash: carry commit identities in the separate launch binding.

Atomic local builder/audit reservations are a new metadata-supervisor custody format, not native claim files. Define them explicitly, with exact phaseapproval/source/spec/claim hashes and unit identities, and preserve exclusive durable creation. They do not replace the native metadata claim or create new campaign slots.

This public clarification permits parsing and source authoring only. It grants no metadata invocation, candidate/oracle import, native task mutation, source implementation access or expiry extension. Record exact supplied text and digest in audit-contract.json actual-input inventory as additive public API material, not as an original frozen input or an implementation read.
